Example of Claude 3.5 Haiku remembering the original objective in detail, but nevertheless stating the competing goal due to the effect of adversarial pressures. ## Appendix E Additional ablations In addition to the ablations described in Section 5, we present the additional results and details. ### E.1 The state complexity hypothesis One of the simplest possibilities for why goal drift might occur under goal switching is that the complexity of the simulation state becomes higher as the length of the instrumental phase increases, due to an increased number of stocks in the agent’s portfolio and higher amounts invested in those stocks. We test the influence of this effect through an ablation where, upon the end of the instrumental phase, we empty the agent’s context window while leaving its portfolio and system message intact. To isolate the effect of portfolio complexity, we do not apply adversarial pressure in this setting. We find that increasing the state complexity has a negligible effect on goal drift scores, producing no significant trend toward increasing goal drift scores as the length of the instrumental phase, and thus the portfolio complexity, increases. Furthermore, this intervention has almost no effect on the $GD_{actions}$ scores.
